learn.title: Last in, first out
learn.body: A stack gives back items in the reverse of the order you added them: last in, first out. Think of a pile of plates. The operations are `push` to add on top and `pop` to remove the top.

learn.title: A stack in an array
learn.body: The array holds the items. `top` is how many are stored, which is also the next free slot.

learn.title: push and pop
learn.body: push stores at `top` then increments. pop decrements then reads.

learn.title: Pushing and popping
steps: Items came out in reverse order

learn.body: Popping an empty stack or pushing onto a full one reads or writes outside the array. That is undefined behaviour. Check `top` first.

questions.explanation: A stack is last in, first out.

questions.prompt: You push 1, then 2, then 3, then pop once. What value comes out?
questions.explanation: The last item pushed is the first popped.

questions.prompt: In the array stack, what does `top` equal right after creation?
questions.explanation: With `top` as the count of items, an empty stack has top 0 and the next free slot is index 0.

questions.prompt: Pushing onto a full array stack writes \_\_ the array.
questions.explanation: The write goes past the last slot, which is undefined behaviour. Check for a full stack first.

questions.prompt: Order the calls so that pop returns 5.
questions.explanation: 5 must be the newest item when pop runs.

questions.prompt: Match each operation to its effect.
questions.explanation: These are the pieces of the array stack.
